decisions.reason: Joshua 10:13 and 2 Samuel 1:18 name a literary work, not a historical man; aligned Hebrew adjectives are the title epithet, not the whole phrase.
The named place Perez-uzzah is attested at 2 Samuel 6:8 and 1 Chronicles 13:11, distinct from Uzzah the man.
The compound Perez-uzzah is a place-name; genuine personal-name tokens including o100060080082 remain untouched.
Three aligned terms in Jeremiah 36:26 and 38:6 mean 'the king' (common noun, not a named man); do not infer one historical individual or kinship.

Genesis 10:14 and 1 Chronicles 1:12 speak of the plural Philistine people; ACAI incorrectly creates one male Philistine. Historical speech-span attributions are not part of the compact index and remain unchanged in the frozen original.
